description: AST-tester probes for Rust — exercises grammar (macros, lifetimes, async traits), chunker, and ranker on idiomatic Rust patterns in astral-sh/ruff.

probes.query: how does ruff classify Python imports into first-party, third-party, and standard-library sections
probes.notes: NL behavior query targeting the isort categorization subsystem. ImportType is the central enum that names all import sections (Future, StandardLibrary, ThirdParty, FirstParty, LocalFolder). The file also carries the categorize() and categorize_imports() functions that implement the classification logic. Exercises chunker on a file with multiple enum/struct definitions and complex lifetime annotations on free functions.

probes.query: how does ruff apply iterative auto-fixes and track the count of applied fixes per rule code
probes.notes: NL behavior query targeting the fix-application loop. lint_fix<'a> is the entry point that iteratively applies fixes until convergence; FixTable tracks per-rule counts. Exercises chunker on a 700-line file that mixes structs, impls, and top-level pub fns, plus the FixerResult<'a> struct that bundles the lifetime-parameterized source-kind borrow.

probes.query: how does ruff walk the Python AST and accumulate lint diagnostics during a single file check
probes.notes: NL behavior query targeting the central AST visitor. Checker<'a> is the AST-visitor state machine that accumulates diagnostics; impl<'a> Visitor<'a> for Checker<'a> at line 945 exercises the impl-for-generic pattern. This is the single largest file in the linter crate and stresses chunker boundary detection when a struct definition spans many fields with lifetime params.

probes.query: Violation trait that all ruff lint rules implement to produce a message and fix availability
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored query. Violation: ViolationMetadata + Sized is the core trait that every lint rule struct implements; AlwaysFixableViolation provides a blanket impl. Exercises chunker on a short file (115 lines) containing two interrelated trait definitions and a blanket impl<V: AlwaysFixableViolation> Violation for V block — a classic pattern parsers may misparse as a struct impl.

probes.query: SemanticSyntaxContext trait defining in_async_context and future_annotations methods for the Python parser
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored query. SemanticSyntaxContext at line 2255 is a large trait (20+ methods) that the parser calls to ask about the surrounding Python AST context. It lives at the bottom of a 2400-line file full of structs, impls, and nested visitor types. Exercises the chunker's ability to correctly delimit a trailing trait definition after long bodies of preceding code.

probes.query: SortedMergeIter struct that merges two sorted iterators by source range position
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored query. SortedMergeIter<L, R, Item> (line 75) and impl<L, R, Item> Iterator for SortedMergeIter ... where Item: Ranged (line 84) are a compact generic struct + trait-impl pair. Exercises the chunker and parser's handling of multi-type-parameter where-clause bounds — a pattern that Rust parsers often misassociate with adjacent items.

probes.query: warn_user_once_by_id macro that suppresses duplicate warnings using a static identifier
probes.notes: Grammar edge-case probe (REQUIRED macro probe). The file defines five consecutive macro_rules! macros (warn_user_once_by_id, warn_user_once_by_message, warn_user_once, warn_user, notify_user) whose bodies contain nested $crate::logging:: paths, use-statements, and format_args invocations. Chunkers that split on brace depth without understanding macro hygiene will misparse the block boundaries and either merge macros or drop the inner use statements.

probes.query: detect_package_root function that walks ancestor directories to find a Python package root path
probes.notes: Grammar edge-case probe (REQUIRED lifetime-param probe). detect_package_root<'a>(path: &'a Path, namespace_packages: &[PathBuf]) -> Option<&'a Path> is a short standalone function (line 36) where the same lifetime 'a threads from input reference to return reference, a pattern that tree-sitter grammars and naive regex-based extractors frequently parse incorrectly when the return type is wrapped in Option<&'a T>.
